references.prompt: A single flat-sided hexagonal diorama tile, 32 m across, lush meadow grass cap and layered soil strata on the hexagon side walls (dark topsoil, red clay, gravel). A straight 8 m wide river runs between one pair of opposite flat edges in a channel cut below the meadow surface with natural earthy banks, clear water tinted pale turquoise in the shallows and deep teal-blue where deep, sun glints, soft caustics on the shallow bed. A 6 m wide two-lane asphalt country road, faded dashed white centre line, low concrete kerbs, grass verges with tufts and small bushes runs straight between another pair of opposite flat edges and crosses the river at 60 degrees on a small single-span stone-faced road bridge with low parapet walls and abutments set into the banks. Where the river meets the tile side wall, the hexagon side wall shows the water column in cross-section like clear tinted resin, turquoise at the top fading to deep blue at the bottom, never an empty gap, stylized-real diorama miniature, real PBR materials, slightly exaggerated proportions, soft noon sun, neutral grey studio background, 35 degree three-quarter view

Close-up of a small single-span stone-faced country road bridge on a diorama tile: the asphalt deck with low kerbs and a faded dashed centre line, low stone parapet walls, abutments set into earthy river banks, the river flowing underneath, clear water tinted pale turquoise in the shallows and deep teal-blue where deep, sun glints, soft caustics on the shallow bed, stylized-real diorama miniature, real PBR materials, slightly exaggerated proportions, soft noon sun, neutral grey studio background, 35 degree three-quarter view

Pending owner re-approval: river_stone, river_reed, river_cattail and bridge_stone bound to the existing masks map, whose texels under the dressing and a 32 px halo around it now carry R 1, G porosity (as the river centres), B 0, A 1, and whose parked causeway block carries (1, 0.8, 0, 1); the road's AO texels are unchanged (compared texel for texel) and so are its mips 0 to 4; the reeds and cattails take the foliage season tint. The GLB is byte-identical, and A = 1 keeps the slots' AO as before (none). At the MVP values, outside each frame's run-to-run noise, at most 54 of 1.6 M isolated pixels differ, by at most 6 levels of 255 in the static frames (up to 23 beside moving agents in the coast checkpoint frames), with no visible change; the one static frame with zero run-to-run noise (the straight coast) shows 6 such pixels, caused by binding the map, while the masked shader math is an identity at those values. Review masks-river-bridge and masks-far, *-before.jpg against *-after.jpg, in docs/checkpoints/hooks/masks-{none,snow,wet,night,autumn}/. Earlier entries stay as history.

Pending owner re-approval; not an approval. Rebuilt for the owner's 2026-10-14 note "cat tails need more close up detail" (eye-level walk mode): LOD0 reed blades and cattails: a 3-sided stalk, a closed 6-sided seed head (flat bottom cap, slight taper, rounded top) and a short pale spike (river_stone slot). Stones, placements, slots and the planar UV0 mapping are unchanged; in the masks map only the dressing's footprint and its halo were rewritten for the new blades, and the road's baked texels and their mips are unchanged (`dress_masks` asserts both); LOD1 keeps four flat triangles per clump along LOD0 blades and LOD2 has no reeds, as before. Tris LOD0/1/2 920/396/120 -> 1766/396/120 (kind center, 4,000, unchanged). Cattail heads on LOD0: 18 before, 18 now (two to four per clump, 31 tris each). Review docs/checkpoints/cattails/ (cattails-before-*.jpg against cattails-after-*.jpg, and clump-{before,after}-{front,back}-lit.jpg). The controller records the owner's decision. Earlier entries stay as history.
